# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary — 2026-08-03

The liquidity hierarchy splits into three distinct tiers. The North American tier—Nasdaq 100 and NYSE—dominates with ILLIQ costs below 0.0060% per $1M traded and comparable volumes exceeding $190.1M, establishing them as unambiguous global liquidity leaders. The second tier comprises Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and London Stock Exchange, which cluster between 0.0295% and 0.0804% per $1M traded but show divergent risk profiles: Tokyo's elevated 2.8369% turnover ratio suggests concentrated activity despite 0.0351% per $1M ILLIQ, while Euronext maintains the tightest AR spread at 0.5454% despite middling volume of $12.7M. The laggards—Korea Exchange, Xetra, and SIX Swiss Exchange—trade higher ILLIQ costs (0.0450% to 0.1539% per $1M), with Korea Exchange notably presenting the worst spread at 1.6569% despite respectable 1.3994% turnover. Xetra and SIX occupy niche positions: both feature competitive AR spreads (0.5934% and 0.5560% respectively) but suffer from minimal comparable volumes ($6.3M and $3.5M), signaling illiquidity driven by market size rather than friction costs.
